weather.tip: 99% rain chance tonight — carry an umbrella and budget extra time on your commute home, especially on stretches that pool water quickly.

around.headline: Road rage: auto driver assaults motorist after minor collision in Banaswadi
around.summary: An auto driver allegedly assaulted a motorist following a minor collision in Bengaluru's Banaswadi. If a fender-bender turns heated, stay in your vehicle with doors locked and call 100 rather than trading blows.

around.headline: Bengaluru woman alleges drunk delivery rider tried to enter her home
around.summary: A woman says a drunk Uber Parcel agent was aggressive and tried to enter her home after a delivery; Uber called the behaviour "unacceptable" and said it is acting on the complaint. Never let a delivery or gig worker inside your home, however routine the ask sounds.

around.headline: Man duped of Rs 4.5 lakh in fake online marble business deal
around.summary: A Bengaluru man lost Rs 4.5 lakh after an online business offer for a marble supply deal turned out to be fraudulent. Treat any unsolicited bulk-trade or supplier deal that demands advance payment before you've met or verified the party as a red flag.

around.headline: BMRCL to energise underground metro's third rail on Reach-6 from August 10
around.summary: Bengaluru Metro will switch on the high-voltage third rail on the Reach-6 underground stretch from August 10 as it races to finish delayed projects. If you're near active construction zones on this stretch, keep clear of trackside barriers once power is live.

around.headline: Bangalore University student's death in road accident sparks protest for campus traffic curbs
around.summary: A Bangalore University student died after being hit by an auto on campus, prompting peers to protest and demand curbs on vehicle traffic within the campus. Expect possible access changes around the campus in the coming days if you commute through or near it.
around.source: The Indian Express, The Times of India

around.headline: Will UPI remain free to use?
around.summary: An explainer examines whether India's free UPI payment system can stay fee-free as transaction volumes and the cost of running the network keep climbing. Any shift here would touch nearly every daily purchase Bengalureans make by QR code.

events.note: Musician Vikram Hazra returns to Bengaluru with a fundraising concert blending music and stillness practices.

street_smart.title: Your bike-taxi crashes and leaves you injured. The driver offers cash on the spot to 'settle it' instead of filing anything. What do you do?
street_smart.based_on: Real incident this week: a Bengaluru woman is seeking Rs 20 lakh compensation from Rapido after a bike-taxi crash left her with a large hospital bill (India Today, News18).
street_smart.situation: You've booked a bike taxi and it collides with another vehicle, throwing you off. You're hurt but conscious. The driver, worried about his account getting flagged, offers you a few thousand rupees in cash right there and asks you to say it's sorted so you both can leave. What do you do?

choices.text: Take the cash — it's quick, and going through the platform or police sounds like a hassle.
choices.feedback: This is the trap. A cash settlement at the roadside doesn't cover a real hospital bill, and by agreeing to 'it's sorted' you give up the paper trail — FIR, medical record, platform report — that ride-app insurance and any compensation claim actually depend on.

choices.text: Argue with the driver about whose fault the crash was before doing anything else.
choices.feedback: Risky. Sorting out blame at the scene wastes the first, most important minutes — getting treated and getting the incident on record matter more right now than winning the argument.

choices.text: Just get up, dust off, and go home since the injury doesn't look too bad.
choices.feedback: Risky. Some injuries (head knocks, internal bruising) don't look serious immediately, and if it worsens later you'll have no accident report or medical timestamp linking it back to the ride.

choices.text: Get medical help if needed, report the crash to the platform and police, and keep the hospital bill and photos as evidence.
choices.feedback: Correct. Ride-hailing apps carry personal accident cover for passengers, but claiming it requires a police report and medical documentation filed close to the time of the incident — not a private cash handshake with the driver.

takeaways: After any ride-hailing accident, call 108 if you're hurt, then file a police complaint the same day — even if the injury looks minor at first.
Report the crash inside the app immediately; most platforms have a time window for accident-cover claims to be valid.
Never accept an on-the-spot cash settlement from a driver in place of a formal report — it forfeits your ability to claim proper medical compensation later.

quiz.question: In which Bengaluru locality did an auto driver allegedly assault a motorist after a minor collision, as reported today?
quiz.why: Road-rage assaults like this can be booked under both the Motor Vehicles Act and criminal assault provisions, not just as a traffic offence.

quiz.question: BMRCL plans to energise the underground metro's high-voltage third rail on which stretch starting August 10?
quiz.why: The third rail carries high-voltage traction power for the trains, which is why safety barriers go up near live tracks once it's switched on.

quiz.question: Journalist Tarun Tejpal was sentenced to how many years in prison in the 2013 sexual assault case?
quiz.why: The case stemmed from an incident at a literary festival that Tejpal himself had founded.

quiz.question: Which organ in the human body produces the hormone insulin?
quiz.why: Insulin helps the body's cells absorb glucose from the bloodstream, keeping blood sugar levels in check.

quiz.question: Which institution regulates currency and monetary policy in India?
quiz.why: The RBI also sets the repo rate, its main lever for controlling inflation across the economy.
